figma.role: Collaborative UI and prototype design tool, with Figma Make turning a prompt or design into a working prototype or app, and AI tools in the editor.
figma.audience: UI and product designers, design students and development teams designing and prototyping together.
pros: Free for students, including Figma Make: higher-education students get the Professional plan free with 3,000 AI credits a month. Figma Make is available to higher-ed and bootcamp Education users.
Monthly credits even on free: a Full seat on Starter gets 500 credits a month, capped at 150 a day. A Full seat on Professional gets 3,000 a month.
Popular by traffic: per a16z's 7th list (Oct 2026, Similarweb Aug 2026 data), Figma is in the top 15 web sites.
cons: Training on content is on by default on Free and Professional: on Starter and Professional content is used to train models by default, and the team admin can turn it off. Off on Organization and Enterprise.
Credits don't roll over: they reset every month. Buying extra credits isn't available on the Education plan.
Free plan is limited in projects: 3 projects and 30-day version history, per the pricing page.
figma.price: Professional from 12 USD per editor per month billed annually, or 15 USD billed monthly. Free plan exists.
figma.free: Free Starter plan: 3 projects, unlimited file storage, 30-day version history, and 500 AI credits a month per Full seat, capped at 150 a day.
plans: Unlimited file storage, 3 projects, 2 members, 30-day version history; 500 credits/month per Full seat, up to 150/day.
Unlimited projects and files, free viewers, team library, private projects; 3,000 credits/month per Full seat and 500 for other seats.
Same as monthly.
Unlimited teams, organization design systems, SSO; 3,500 credits/month per Full seat.
figma.privacy: Per the help center, Figma uses content to train models when the Content training setting is on. On Starter and Professional it is on by default and the team admin can turn it off; on Organization and Enterprise it is off. Figma doesn't use Figma for Education account data for training. Training took effect 15 Aug 2024.
figma.students: Figma for Education is free: students in higher education, approved bootcamps and high school get the Professional plan with 3,000 AI credits a month. Figma Make is only for higher-ed Education users.
figma.watch: In Figma Make users report 3,000 credits run out in about 3 days, mostly on fixing the AI's mistakes.

framer.role: Visual website builder with AI agents, a content system, hosting and multilingual support.
framer.audience: Designers, students and freelancers building marketing sites and portfolios without code.
pros: A free year for students: students get the Basic plan free for a year, with 1,000 AI credits a month, for a personal site, portfolio and coursework.
Right-to-left site support: since 2 Oct 2025 Framer automatically flips Stacks and Grids layouts in RTL languages, and the update names Hebrew explicitly.
Credits renew even on free: the free plan has 500 AI credits a month, a free Framer domain and 1GB bandwidth.
cons: Your own domain only when paid: on Free the site publishes on a Framer domain.
Extra editors cost extra: an extra editor is 20 USD/month and a content editor 10 USD/month. Viewers are free.
Automatic RTL flipping is partial: it applies only to Stacks and Grids, and existing projects need it enabled manually in settings.
framer.price: From 10 USD/month (Basic plan). Free plan with 500 AI credits a month.
framer.free: Free plan: 500 AI credits a month, a free Framer domain, 1GB bandwidth and 1,000 pages.
plans: 500 AI credits/month, free Framer domain, 1GB bandwidth, 1,000 pages, 10 CMS collections, uploads up to 5MB, one extra language.
Tiers of 1,000 to 15,000 credits/month (price rises with the tier).
Tiers of 3,000 to 100,000 credits/month.
framer.privacy: Per the AI Notice (v1.2, effective 18 Sep 2026), on non-Enterprise plans the user grants Framer a license to use input and output to train its models, unless training is turned off in workspace settings. No training on Enterprise. External model providers may not train on input and output.
framer.rights: Per the AI Notice, input and output are the customer's 'Content' and the customer is responsible for it; Framer holds rights in the AI tools and usage data, not the output.
framer.hebrew: Sites: an official update of 2 Oct 2025 mentions Hebrew and Arabic and adds automatic RTL layout flipping. Interface language: not mentioned in source.
framer.students: Basic plan free for a year (valued at 120 USD on the page) and 1,000 AI credits a month, for a personal site only. Needs an institutional email and a photo of a student ID; review takes up to 5 business days; can be renewed every 11 months.

relume.role: AI workspace that plans a sitemap and wireframes and builds a site from them, with a component library for Webflow and Figma and site hosting.
relume.audience: Web designers, freelancers and agencies, mainly those working with Webflow or Figma.
pros: A whole site on the free plan: per the FAQ, the free plan includes enough monthly AI use to build a full site, with free hosting at relumesite.ai.
Commercial use allowed: asked whether you can use it in commercial projects, the pricing page answers 'You sure can!'.
Editors without per-seat charges: you can invite anyone to the workspace as an editor with no per-seat fee.
cons: Branding and limits on the free site: free sites show a Relume badge and are limited to 20 form submissions a month and 7 days of analytics.
Confusing pricing structure: the page shows both a workspace Pro and a Site Builder Pro at different prices, with no numeric credit quotas.
relume.price: Workspace Pro from 24 USD/month, and site hosting from 12 USD per project per month billed annually. Free plan exists.
relume.free: Free forever, no credit card: monthly AI use enough to build a full site, hosting at relumesite.ai, 20 form submissions a month and 7 days of analytics.
relume.trial: The FAQ mentions a 7-day trial of Pro.
plans: Monthly AI use enough for a full site, hosting at relumesite.ai, 20 form submissions/month, 7 days of analytics.
Starts at 1 to 2 sites a month.
Hosting for one site.
Hosting for one site.
relume.rights: The pricing page answers 'You sure can!' on commercial projects. Ownership of generated content isn't explained; license terms not read.
relume.watermark: Sites on the free plan show a Relume badge.
relume.students: The pricing page mentions no student discount.

google-stitch.role: Google Labs tool that creates UI designs for apps and sites from a prompt, on an infinite canvas with a design agent and interactive prototypes.
google-stitch.audience: Designers, students and developers who want fast design directions and UI prototypes.
google-stitch.status: Active. The official site presents the product as 'Stitch (Beta)'.
pros: From idea to prototype on one canvas: the 18 March 2026 update added an infinite canvas, a design agent that knows the whole project history, and prototypes you can run with a Play button.
Design system from any site: extract a design system from any URL, and import or export design rules in a DESIGN.md file.
Connection to dev tools: an MCP server, an SDK and skills, and export to AI Studio and Antigravity.
cons: Beta product: the official site shows it as 'Stitch (Beta)'.
No official quota information: the official pages checked publish no price, usage quotas or list of available countries.
google-stitch.api: Yes. Per the official blog, Stitch offers an MCP server, an SDK and skills, and export to AI Studio and Antigravity. Terms and prices not checked.

ux-pilot.role: AI tool that creates wireframes and UI designs from a prompt.
ux-pilot.audience: UX designers and product managers who want wireframes and first screens fast.
pros: You can start free: per the pricing page there is a free plan for wireframes and AI design, no credit card.
cons: Plan details not published on the accessible page: plan names, credit quotas and billing type didn't appear, and FAQ answers were empty.
ux-pilot.price: Paid plans from 14 USD/month per the pricing page. Free plan exists.
ux-pilot.free: Free plan, no credit card: 80 credits a day and one project, with the main design tools (wireframes, full UI, prototype, design review).
plans: 80 credits/day, one project, main design tools.
ux-pilot.students: The pricing page mentions no student discount.

v0.role: Vercel agent that builds UIs, sites and web apps from a text prompt, with visual editing and publishing on Vercel.
v0.audience: Developers, designers and founders who want to turn an idea into a working UI or web app.
pros: From prompt to published site: even the free plan includes publishing on Vercel, visual editing in Design Mode and GitHub sync.
Daily credits on paid plans: Plus and Business include 30 USD in credits a month per user, plus 2 USD in free credits each day you sign in.
Work on existing code: since the 3 Feb 2026 release, v0 can import an existing GitHub repo, create a branch per chat and open a PR that deploys on merge.
cons: Daily limit on the free plan: Free allows up to 7 messages a day.
Training on your data by default on free: free v0 users with a Vercel Hobby account are included in model training by default; opt out in team settings.
v0.price: From 30 USD per user per month (Plus). Free plan with up to 7 messages a day.
v0.free: Free plan: access to v0, publishing on Vercel, Design Mode and GitHub sync, limited to 7 messages a day.
plans: Access to v0, Vercel publishing, Design Mode, GitHub sync, up to 7 messages/day.
30 USD in credits/month per user, plus 2 USD in credits per day on sign-in.
v0.privacy: Per Vercel's 17 Mar 2026 terms update, v0 users on Free or Premium with a Vercel Hobby account are included in model training by default; other v0 users are excluded by default. Opt out in Team Settings under Data Preferences. Data shared before opting out isn't returned.
v0.students: The pricing page links 'v0 for Students' and has an FAQ on student discounts, but the answer is empty. Terms not verified.

webflow.role: Platform for designing, building and hosting professional websites, with AI tools for building a site from a prompt, writing and SEO.
webflow.audience: Web designers and developers, freelancers and agencies building professional sites with a content system.
webflow.status: Active. Webflow's student program was discontinued.
pros: Start free with AI: the Starter site plan is free and includes Webflow AI, MCP server access, 2 static pages and a webflow.io domain. A free workspace gets 200 AI credits a month.
No training on customer content: per Webflow, it doesn't use customer data to train generative models, and agreements with model providers bar them from training on the data.
Varied AI tools: the pricing page lists building a site from a prompt, generating design sections, generating code components, writing content and improving SEO and AEO.
cons: No student discount anymore: Webflow for Students ended on 28 Feb 2026 with no replacement. The alternative is the free Starter plan.
Limited free plan: Starter has 2 static pages, 1GB bandwidth and 50 form submissions, and can't publish to a custom domain.
Dual pricing: you pay separately for a site plan and a workspace plan, plus editor seats (a Full seat is 39 USD/month billed annually).
webflow.price: Site plan from 15 USD/month billed annually (Basic). Free Starter plan with a webflow.io domain.
webflow.model: Site and workspace subscription, with AI credits
webflow.free: Starter site plan and Starter workspace plan are free: webflow.io domain, 2 static pages, 1GB bandwidth, 50 form submissions, Webflow AI and 200 AI credits a month.
plans: webflow.io domain, limited CMS, 2 static pages, 1GB bandwidth, 50 form submissions, Webflow AI and MCP server, hosting for 5 apps on Webflow Cloud.
For simple sites without a CMS.
For content-rich sites with a CMS and higher traffic.
200 AI credits/month.
300 AI credits/month.
300 AI credits/month.
400 AI credits/month.
400 AI credits/month.
webflow.privacy: Per Webflow's AI access page, Webflow doesn't use customer data to train generative models, and prompts and output aren't used to improve foundation models. Agreements with external providers bar them from training on the data. Workspace admins can turn AI features off.
webflow.rights: The page read doesn't address ownership of output and points to product terms, which weren't read.
webflow.api: Not verified. The pricing page mentions MCP server access on site plans. API docs not checked.
webflow.students: Webflow for Students was discontinued on 28 Feb 2026 with no planned replacement. Those who got a discount before keep it to the end of the term. The alternative is the free Starter plan.

wix.role: Website builder with hosting, a store and appointment booking, including Wix Harmony, an AI website builder with the Aria agent.
wix.audience: Small businesses, creators and students who want a site with hosting and a store without code.
pros: AI building and manual editing in one tool: Wix Harmony, announced 21 Jan 2026, combines creating a site from a prompt with drag editing. The Aria agent is at its center.
Free plan, no credit card: the Free plan costs 0 USD and includes hosting and a drag editor.
Right-to-left sites: Wix Multilingual lets you set menu, text and images right-to-left per language.
cons: Own domain and removing branding only when paid: per the FAQ, connecting your own domain and removing Wix branding need a paid plan.
Shown prices are annual, paid upfront: prices on the page are for an annual subscription paid in full at purchase, and the offer applies only to the first term.
Partial right-to-left support: per the help center, only some site elements can be set right-to-left, such as strips, presentations and repeaters.
wix.price: From 17 USD/month billed annually upfront (Light). Free plan exists.
wix.free: Free plan, no cost and no credit card: hosting and a drag editor. Your own domain and removing branding need a paid plan.
plans: Site hosting and a drag editor.
2GB storage, 2 site collaborators, a free domain for a year, basic marketing suite.
50GB storage, 5 collaborators, a free domain for a year, accepting payments, basic store, appointment booking.
wix.privacy: Per Wix's generative AI policy, content users create, such as images and page layouts, is one data source under the terms of use license, and data is also collected to train Wix software tools including AI and machine-learning models. The page doesn't describe an opt-out and doesn't explicitly mention prompts.
wix.rights: Per a Wix blog post of 19 Oct 2026, Wix doesn't claim ownership of output, and materials generated in the account belong to the user; templates and design code are licensed.
wix.watermark: Sites on the free plan show Wix branding, and removing it needs a paid plan.
wix.api: Not verified. Per the plans page Business Elite includes an 'advanced developer platform'. API docs not checked.
wix.hebrew: Sites: Wix Multilingual supports right-to-left sites per language, but the article read doesn't mention Hebrew by name. Per the press release, Wix Harmony started rolling out in English. Interface language: not mentioned in source.
wix.students: No official student benefit found. The plans page mentions no student discount.
wix.watch: Users report it's hard to move a site and domain out, and renewals at a high price without notice.
